title: How Tunas Evolved to Become an Apex Predator of the Sea
gist: A Proceedings of the Royal Society B study using DNA from more than 50 Scombridae species refutes the prevailing view that tunas became apex predators by filling the ecological vacuum left by the dinosaur-killing asteroid. The clade did originate near the 66-million-year-old impact, but its defining warm-blooded traits evolved much later, decoupling the extinction event from the trait innovation.

insights.claim: Tunas are among the rare animals that keep their bodies warmer than the surrounding environment, and that endothermy gives them a physiological advantage in generating and sustaining energy that underpins their top-predator role.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: A trait-based rather than opportunity-based explanation for ecological dominance is the same logic investors apply to durable competitive advantage: capability, not vacated market space.
